review.outcome: ShipLoop delivered and committed the requested greeting, unittest and preserved checkpoint, but the E2E run failed its independent missing-completion contract check.

learnings.title: Restore continuation while the required completion is missing
learnings.evidence: S-2 and S-10: shiploop-hook-contract-receipt.json records three allow/no-progress decisions for active_loop_missing_done, with unchanged product, state, receipt and loop-state hashes; each response omitted the current action and done command. The tested scripts/shiploop_keepalive.py:577-582 explicitly allows stopping on unchanged progress. Contrary evidence: the live run's trace.jsonl:39 continued at implement revision 13, and :86 allowed stopping only after done.
learnings.proposal: Carry this evidence into LR-20261101-58f651 and its existing restoration candidate. Keep a valid active action awaiting its required completion under script control, and return its exact recovery/completion instructions without restarting the loop or replaying writes. Preserve explicit stop, blocked, terminal and ownership handling. This run alone does not qualify the candidate.
learnings.premise_note: S-1, S-2 and S-10 remain authoritative: scripts determine continuation and acceptance; neither elapsed effort nor the model's final message completes the action.

optimizations.title: Print executable loop recovery and reporting commands
optimizations.evidence: S-4 and S-5: events.jsonl:189 parses a receipt and executes next_argv through model-written Python. Similar wrappers recur at events 63, 90, 120, 156, 246, 273, 294 and 325. Event 225 extracts an action value from done_argv using command substitution and assembles the completion command. scripts/shiploop_loops.py:497-501 and :521-540 instruct the model to run those arrays. metrics.model_glue is zero despite these directly observed wrappers.
optimizations.proposal: Investigate a thin ShipLoop adapter that prints or executes exact receipt-bound recovery and reporting commands through the existing Until Loop runtime. Keep judgments model-authored, but move argument extraction and command assembly into scripts. Measure any savings separately from the hook-restoration candidate.
optimizations.premise_note: S-1 and S-12 require reuse of the existing runtime's action identity, validation and acceptance logic; the adapter must not create another navigator or loop implementation.

optimizations.title: Remove instructions to compose progress updates
optimizations.evidence: S-15: scripts/shiploop_prompts.py:357-359 asks for one line 'of your own', and :512 asks for a line per stage. Transcript lines 39, 99, 117, 176 and 199 contain model-composed progress. metrics.narrative records 23 emitted narratives, 19 shown, 18 verbatim and 22 of 23 accepted results with headlines.
optimizations.proposal: Align the shared progress instruction and SKILL.md with script-rendered status: show the script's text unchanged when the host has not displayed it, once per milestone, without adding a composed substitute. Preserve host display handling and suppress unchanged repeats.
optimizations.premise_note: S-15 assigns status rendering to scripts. This wording correction preserves script navigation and the grounding required by S-6 and S-7.

discoveries.title: One successful live continuation does not exercise unchanged-progress completion

evidence.observation: All three repeated fixture decisions allowed stopping with no progress; current-action and done-command instructions were absent. Recorded snapshots remained unchanged.
evidence.interpretation: The installed build retains a reproducible completion-contract defect even though this particular live action recovered.

evidence.observation: The live hook continued once, recovery returned the same action and loop, and the final allow decision followed engine completion.
evidence.interpretation: The live result is useful contrary evidence against a blanket claim that continuation is broken, but it does not refute the narrower unchanged-progress failure.

mission_anchor.challenge: No amendment is proposed. S-1 and S-10 also require the unfinished action to remain under script control.

discoveries.potential_impact: An unattended attempt can end before its required callback; the independent check already changed this run's overall verdict to failed.
alternatives: The existing progress-based continuation suffices when the first premature stop follows recorded progress, as it did live here.
The fixture establishes the narrow mechanism failure; its frequency in ordinary model behavior is unknown.
discoveries.next_experiment: First replay an active action with unchanged progress and a missing done against the existing restoration candidate, checking exact action identity and unchanged product/loop state. Then exercise repeated premature finals live. A replay cannot qualify E2E benefit: retain prospective promotion/5, one learning record per candidate, and exposing-plus-another-style coverage or an explicitly narrower claim.
discoveries.proposal: Attach this recurrence and its live-success counterexample to the existing restoration investigation and candidate; do not open or bundle a second hook fix.

discoveries.title: Receipt arrays leave mechanical command assembly to the model

evidence.observation: The model parsed next_argv for recovery and extracted an action argument from done_argv for reporting; the printed instructions direct it to those arrays.
evidence.interpretation: The runtime supplies authoritative values, but the handoff still requires mechanical glue rather than a command the model can copy.

evidence.observation: Both counters are zero despite the observed wrappers, and the run completed.
evidence.interpretation: The interface burden is demonstrated; a reliability or efficiency gain from removing it has not yet been measured. The frozen glue counter is not exhaustive.

mission_anchor.challenge: No amendment is proposed. S-5 assigns the assembly to scripts, while S-12 forbids duplicating the runtime.

discoveries.potential_impact: Copy-ready commands could reduce quoting mistakes and repeated wrapper construction; this run establishes no saved turns or avoided failure.
alternatives: A host with direct argv execution may consume the existing arrays without shell glue.
Rendering exact commands may suffice without adding a dispatch adapter.
discoveries.next_experiment: Give a cold consumer only an active-loop recovery packet and then a reporting packet. Compare exact command rendering with the current arrays, including spaces in paths and stale action IDs. Require identical runtime acceptance and no restart; qualify any broader gain separately from hook restoration.
discoveries.proposal: Investigate command rendering before adding an adapter, preserving the existing loop runtime and script-issued identities.

discoveries.title: Progress guidance contradicts the script-rendered reporting contract

evidence.observation: The guidance combines exact narrative display with instructions to provide model-authored progress.
evidence.interpretation: The engine supplies conflicting reporting duties rather than consistently enforcing S-15.

evidence.observation: Authored updates occurred; only 18 of 23 emitted narratives were recorded as shown verbatim.
evidence.interpretation: The contradiction was accompanied by reporting deviations, although its causal contribution has not been isolated.

mission_anchor.challenge: No amendment is proposed; retain script-rendered status and existing host display routes.

discoveries.potential_impact: Users may receive omitted or paraphrased progress despite an available saved-state narrative; delivery correctness was unaffected here.
alternatives: Some omissions may be host-display or narrative-detection limitations.
Model attention may also contribute independently of the contradictory wording.
discoveries.next_experiment: Check emitted instructions for host-displayed and model-displayed status, then run a focused live milestone sequence. Verify exact text, no duplicate display and no composed substitute. Treat any full-run efficiency claim as requiring separate qualification.
discoveries.proposal: Remove the model-composition directive and state one consistent script-display rule while retaining all stage grounding.

learning_retention.answer: Keep the existing append-only learning records and verbose operator-owned learning commits. Record this failed attempt even though its product passed. This read-only review does not create that commit or establish the required independent judge assessment.
proposals: Append this recurrence to LR-20261101-58f651, retaining both the fixture failure and successful live continuation with their distinct evidence scopes.
Preserve the raw rollout: transcript.md:159 combines the checkpoint and subsequent commentary, while rollout line 505 establishes that the checkpoint itself was an exact final-channel message.

The operator should inspect full relevant source history before admitting separate changes, record the required learning commit, and obtain a fresh judge assessment bound to this review's exact bytes. Those actions remain pending outside this review.

further_learning.answer: The useful remaining distinction is between recovery after recorded progress and recovery when completion is still missing without new progress. Cold-context behavior and other task styles remain unobserved.
proposals: Exercise repeated premature endings during the same active action, checking that completed writes are not replayed and loops are not restarted (S-2, S-6, S-10).
Use a contrasting non-smoke task family for qualification; preserve independent product checks and owned-resource cleanup (S-8, S-9, S-13).
Do not use this overlapped attempt for a wall-time improvement claim. Keep token totals, unknown dollar cost and timing validity distinct.

evaluation_criteria.answer: The existing criteria correctly failed this run. No relaxed floor or new universal metric is justified; improve the precision of evidence attribution and exercise the missing conditions.
proposals: Continue distinguishing live checkpoint behavior from the selected-package synthetic contract receipt; neither substitutes for the other (S-9).
Retain explicit observations for action identity, missing done, preserved writes and loop continuity; do not treat final checkpoint bytes alone as proof of recovery (S-1, S-2, S-6).
Keep heuristic zero counts from being interpreted as full conformance: observed command glue and authored status remain reviewable facts despite counters (S-4, S-5, S-15).

Leave mutation discrimination, fresh-context equivalence and cross-style generality unobserved until exercised; packet size and review counts are diagnostics, not optimization targets (S-6, S-7, S-9, S-10, S-13).
